verses.1: And the children of Israel did evil in the eyes of Jehovah. Therefore, Jehovah handed them over to Midian for seven years.
verses.2: And Midian’s hands were set against Israel. The children of Israel built for them canals along the rivers, as well as cities and fortresses.
verses.3: And if the Israelites were to sow their seeds, and they would rise up against them from Dan and Amalek, and from the children of Canaan.
verses.4: They camped there, and they destroyed the crops of the land until the time of Azah. They didn’t leave any life in Israel, either in Yehuda or Samaria.
verses.5: For they and their flocks will come up from their homes, and they will enter the land in great numbers. There is no end to their numbers. They will come into the land to destroy it.
verses.6: And Israel was defeated greatly by Midian. And the sons of Israel cried out to Jehovah for help.
verses.7: And it happened that the children of Israel cried out to Jehovah about the destruction of Midian.
verses.8: And Jehovah sent a prophet to the children of Israel. He said to them, “As it is written, ‘Jehovah, the God of Israel, says: I have brought you out of Egypt, and I will free you from being slaves.’”
verses.9: And I will rescue you from Egypt, and from all your enemies. I will free you from your troubles, and I will give you your land.
verses.10: And she said to you, “I am Jehovah your God. Do not fear the gods of the Amorites, who live in their land. Nor listen to their voices.”
verses.11: And the angel of the LORD came and sat down under the rod in the wilderness, where my father Abraham was held captive. And Isaac was working in the field to prepare grain for food from before Midian.
verses.12: And the LORD appeared to him and said, “YHWH is with you; may the power of life be upon you.”
verses.13: And Gideon said to him, “My Lord, surely Jehovah is with us. Why have you brought us through all this? And what are all these disasters that our ancestors told us about? They said, ‘We were taken captive from Egypt by Jehovah.’ Now, Lord, abandon us, and give us back our land.”
verses.14: And Jehovah spoke to him, “Use your strength to save Israel from Midian. After all, you were sent here to do this.”
verses.15: And he said to him, “In my hands is the salvation of Israel. Look, there are thousands of poor people among the people, and I am just a young man in my father’s house.”
verses.16: And the LORD said to him, “If I be with you, and you take Midian as one man.”
verses.17: And he said to him, “If only I could please your eyes, and you would do whatever I ask of you.”
verses.18: Please do not leave me here until you come back. I have brought my offerings and laid them before you. He said, “I will stay here until you return.”
verses.19: And Gideon came and made a pit for the sheep. He placed the sheep in the pit, and he set up a fence around it. Then he went down to the bottom of the pit and entered there.
verses.20: And Melchizedek said to him, “Take the grain and the oil, and carry them to the altar. Also, take the bitter ointment and use it as prescribed.” And he did as he was told.
verses.21: And the angel of the LORD sent out his sickle over the field. He hit the plants and the vines. The fire flowed from the stalks, and it consumed the plants and the vines. Then the angel of the LORD left his place.
verses.22: And Gideon saw that it was indeed the angel of the LORD. He said, “Oh Lord, my God! For now I have seen the angel of the LORD face to face.”
verses.23: And the LORD said to him, “Shalom to you. Do not fear; do not die.”
verses.24: And there he built a altar for Jehovah. Jehovah called it “Shalom.” To this day, it remains standing on the hill of my father, my helper.
verses.25: And in that night, Jehovah said to him, “Take the fruit of your father’s orchard, and also the fruit of the second year, which you have planted. You destroyed the altar of the god who was dedicated by your father. And also destroy everything that was associated with that altar.”
verses.26: And you built a altar for the LORD your God on top of this altar. Then you took the second fruit and placed it on the branches of the olive tree that were designated as sacred.
verses.27: And Gadon took twelve men from his servants, and he did as the LORD commanded him. He feared the house of his father and the people of the city because of their actions during the day. So he acted accordingly at night.
verses.28: In the morning, the people of the city gathered together. And they saw that the statue of the god had been destroyed. The flower that was placed on top of the statue had also been removed.
verses.29: And they said to each other, “Who could have done such a thing?” They searched for an answer and finally said, “Gideon son of Joash did this.”
verses.30: And the people of the city said to Yoash, “Bring out your offerings! For you have destroyed the idol of Baal, and you have also killed the priest who stood before it.”
verses.31: And Yoash said to all those who stood against him, “You shall fight against the man who opposes you. If you defeat him, he will die by morning. But if God helps him, then he will be able to destroy our idols.”
verses.32: And that day, Yerubal was called upon. He said, “May the Lord bless him, for he has destroyed the idol.”
verses.33: And all of Midian, Amalek, and the children of Canaan gathered together. They crossed over and camped at the valley of Jezreel.
verses.34: And the Spirit of Jehovah watered the wheat, and it was planted in the field. Then Abiyazer cried out in pain.
verses.35: And the angels sent them to every man. He also cried out after them. The angels sent them to Asher, Zebulun, and Naftali. And they went to carry out their commands.
verses.36: And Gideon said to the Lord, “If You will indeed save Israel with Your hand, as You have spoken.”
verses.37: Now, I will show you the state of the vineyard. If it remains barren and empty, then I know that Israel will be saved by my hand, just as you said.
verses.38: And so it happened. They rose from the night, and they rushed towards the cliff. They poured out rain from the cliff, a mixture of mud and water.
verses.39: And Gideon said to the Lord, “Do not harm me.” But this time, I will try once more. Please, let it be just once. Let it be a disaster for the Philistines alone. And over all the land, there shall be destruction.
verses.40: And God did so that night. There was a great destruction in the land, and all over the earth there was chaos.
